title: decode_uuencode truncation heuristic (data.len() >= limit) is fragile API contract
description: In mime-tree/src/decode.rs decode_uuencode, the caller distinguishes 'stopped at limit' from 'genuine decode error' by checking block.data.len() >= limit. This works because decode_limited() guarantees data.len() <= max_bytes. But this invariant is not documented on DecodedBlock or decode_limited(), and it's easy to break: if decode_limited() is ever changed to return data.len() < limit when stopping at the limit (e.g., to avoid a partial UU group), the heuristic silently misclassifies the result as is_encoding_problem. Better design: decode_limited() should return an explicit StopReason enum (LimitReached | EndFound | DecodeError | NoBeginLine) so callers don't have to infer cause from data length. Or add a was_limit_reached: bool field to DecodedBlock. Current heuristic works but only because of an undocumented invariant coupling two separate modules.
close_reason: Added comment documenting the data.len()>=limit invariant coupling and its fragility. Also corrected false O(max_bytes) comment in decode_uuencode.
